We have $∇\cdot G=-4z.$
First, we express our triple integral as a repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}∇\cdot G\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}-4z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

Since the domain of integration $R=[0,2]\times [0,2]\times [0,4]$ is a rectangular box, and the integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}-4z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}-2\cdot 2z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & =-2{\int }_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{0}^{4}2z\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{\int }_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{0}^{4}2z\,\text{d}z & =-2[x]_{0}^{2}\cdot [y]_{0}^{2}\cdot [{z}^{2}]_{0}^{4} \\  & =-2\cdot (2-0)\cdot (2-0)\cdot (16-0) \\  & =-128.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note**: This is equal to the answer found in step 2. This is not a coincidence! It is a consequence of the so-called divergence theorem. If you haven't met the divergence theorem yet, don't worry, you will soon.
